PROJECT MANAGEMENT APPLICATION · 11 NOVEMBER 2026

System handover and user manual

Project allocation · Role workflows · Financial boundaries · Test evidence

How to use this manual

This handover explains how the Project Management application moves work from project creation to assignment, delivery and oversight. It is intended for administrators, centre leaders, project managers and end users. Follow the numbered project workflow first, then use the role guide for daily work.

Release review date: 11 November 2026. Author: st10466840. Screenshots use disposable demonstration records, not production data. Existing CSS, colours, page layouts and button styling are preserved.

Validation result: 242 automated tests passed. Browser checks passed project creation, team assignment, task creation, staff update and persistence after reload. These are developer-executed acceptance checks; business-owner UAT approval is still required before production acceptance.

Project delivery workflow

The project lead owns coordination. Team membership makes a person eligible for task assignment; assigning a task gives them work to update. Centre Heads can work across projects in their centre. Overseers perform the equivalent nonfinancial oversight. Financial Admins require their own or explicitly allocated work.

Task states are To Do → In Progress → Review → Done. Project status and task status are separate fields. Review and completion decisions should follow the centre’s operating process.

Create the project

  1. Open Manage & Load Projects (centre leadership) or Assign (Project Manager).
  2. Choose New Project. Enter a name, description, project type and status. Set a due date when offered.
  3. Choose Create. Open the project using View. Confirm that the saved project appears in the workspace.
  4. For books, New Book Project also supports a lead author and planned chapters. Keep the linked book tracker aligned with the project.

Overseers cannot select or submit the Financial / Client Bid project type. Do not use financial names or values in ordinary project descriptions to bypass this boundary.

Assign responsibility

  1. Select the project with View.
  2. Choose an eligible person under Project Lead / Project Manager and press Assign Project Lead.
  3. Select a team member, describe their responsibility, then press Assign Member.
  4. Check the assigned-individuals list. Remove withdraws a team allocation; confirm the intended effect on delivery before using it.
  5. Under Add Task, enter a title, select an assigned team member, priority, task type, status and due date. Submit the task form.

The assignee list is limited to the project team. If a person is missing, assign them to the project first. An email warning does not undo a saved allocation: check the assigned list before retrying.

Update and track delivery

  1. The assigned staff member opens Kanban Board.
  2. Find the assigned task and choose Update. Set the status and enter a progress comment.
  3. Choose Save Update. Wait for the save to finish, then reload and confirm the state remains.
  4. Managers use their editable Kanban to edit task details or move cards. Centre Heads and admins can also edit financial work through the financial Kanban.
  5. Leadership uses Team Monitoring Kanban, Overview and Gantt Chart to track assignments, due dates and progress. The monitoring board is a viewing workspace; use the editable board for changes.

Administrator user guide

Manage users, create projects, allocate leads and teams, monitor delivery, administer finance and inspect security activity.

Use Manage Users for account administration. Use Manage & Load Projects for allocation. Open Financial Projects and My task Kanban for financial delivery. Personal My Projects remains assignment based.

Centre Head user guide

Manage the centre’s projects, teams, publications and CRM; inspect centre activity; use finance and edit the financial Kanban.

Financial Projects → My task Kanban permits edits and status changes. Research-centre scope remains enforced. Cost-centre creation and conversion remain restricted to roles already allowed to perform them.

Overseer user guide

Centre Head equivalent for nonfinancial centre work, publications, allocation, monitoring, activity and security review.

Open PM Tools, Research Projects and nonfinancial CRM tabs. Finance, financial projects, bids, financial Kanban, monetary CRM figures, financial reports and exports are hidden or denied. Direct URLs do not grant access.

Project Manager user guide

Create and coordinate owned or assigned projects, allocate staff, edit tasks, maintain publications and engagement notes.

Use Assign → New Project → View → Assign Member. Use Kanban Board for task edits. e-Learning and Templates provide shared resources. Publication work remains subject to scope.

Financial Admin user guide

Manage owned financial opportunities, applied bids, engagement notes and allocated delivery tasks; maintain permitted finance records.

Use Financial Projects, Applied Bids, My Project Kanban and Finance. Paper and Books links are hidden from the manager navigation. Keep financial pipeline stages distinct from task delivery status.

Staff user guide

Update personally assigned tasks, maintain daily work and access assignments and shared resources.

Use Kanban Board → Update → Save Update. Home supports daily-work completion and reopening. Assignments shows project membership; it does not grant access to colleagues’ personal task lists.

Dean user guide

Review institutional overview, monitoring, CRM and detailed read-only finance.

Use Detailed Finance Overview for financial inspection. Publication screens currently expose some mutation buttons that reject the Dean role; see known limitations. Do not rely on those buttons for approvals.

Student user guide

Maintain the student profile, submit documents, reply to feedback and request meetings.

Use the dashboard submission and meeting forms. Open available submission files and feedback attachments. Supervisor allocation controls who can review the student’s record.

Supervisor user guide

View assigned students and student conversations in the dedicated supervisor portal.

Use My Students / the portal dashboard, open the student detail and use messages. Use the dedicated portal rather than the legacy admin supervisor layout, whose access checks remain inconsistent.

Financial work and access boundaries

Financial Admins, admins and Centre Heads can open the financial board. Admins can edit financial-project tasks without receiving blanket access to unrelated personal tasks. Centre Heads can edit tasks within their centre. Financial Admins retain ownership and allocation restrictions.

Save a task with Edit, update details and submit. Move a card to a valid status column to save its status. Reload to confirm persistence. Invalid statuses and malformed requests must fail without changing the task. Cross-centre and unallocated records remain restricted.

Overseers have no financial board access. Their overview excludes financial projects, cost-centre cards and the client pipeline. Nonfinancial CRM tabs retain their existing presentation while monetary figures and financial report tabs are withheld.

Other daily features

Publications

Authorized authors and project roles use Paper and Book trackers for research outputs. Add the output, assign contributors or reviewers where offered, maintain its status and attach the relevant document. Chapter administration requires manager or centre leadership permissions; author participation does not imply permission to administer every chapter.

Communique and shared resources

Communique contains notices and downloadable templates. Upload controls are limited to authorized administrators. e-Learning and Templates provide shared reference material through the relevant role workspace.

Daily work and reports

Staff choose their assigned work on Home and use Complete or Reopen to maintain the daily list. Weekly reports record project progress; review scope depends on the user’s role and project allocation.

Security confirmation

If an unusual-login review appears, choose the confirmation action only when the activity is yours. Confirmation records the review and dismisses the matching personal alert. If it is unfamiliar, use the account-security/password-change path. Administrators retain their own security audit records.

Staff task creation and delegation

Staff can now create tasks in projects assigned directly to them or through project team membership. Open Project Tasks in the sidebar, or View projects and add tasks on the personal Kanban. Choose View tasks and add task, complete the Add Task form and select Create Task.

The form submits to the same task-creation endpoint as the project manager. It records the staff member as creator, links the task to the selected project and permits delegation only to a current project team member or the directly assigned project lead. The shared project task table shows title, assignee, creator, status, due date and progress. Project stakeholders can open this view; personal Kanban boards continue to show assigned personal work.

Unassigned staff cannot open or create tasks for another project. Outside assignees and parent tasks from another project are rejected without saving. Validation errors remain on the staff form without exposing project allocation controls.

Five added regression tests cover shared-endpoint creation and stakeholder visibility, unassigned access denial, outside assignee and parent-task validation, direct assignment, and invalid-form handling. All 242 tests passed. These additional checks are automated regression checks; the previous browser acceptance results describe the earlier manager-led workflow.

Notification bell

Select the bell in the top right corner to open recent notifications. Select a notification to mark it read; the unread count updates for your account. Full notification text is shown in the panel. Account Security opens the security review page. Escape or clicking outside closes the panel. If loading fails, use Retry.

The shared bell is present for administrators, centre heads, overseers, project managers, financial admins, staff, deans, students and supervisors. It refreshes on opening and every 30 seconds. The panel opens without depending on Bootstrap JavaScript. Reading uses a protected POST request and a per-user receipt.

Browser checks passed opening, marking read, Escape and outside-click closing for all nine roles with Bootstrap JavaScript blocked. The full regression suite passes 242 tests.

Deployment and operations handover

  1. Back up the database and media. Install the application requirements in the target environment.
  2. Apply database migrations, including users migration 0006. This adds the Overseer role choice without changing existing users.
  3. An administrator assigns Overseer to the intended accounts and selects their research centre. Do not grant a finance role through another account as a workaround.
  4. Run application checks and the test suite in the test environment. Confirm authentication, static assets, email and uploads in staging.
  5. Configure Blob storage only when wanted: set AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING and AZURE_CONTAINER, create the container, and verify uploads and downloads. A full Azurite connection string must use an endpoint reachable by the application and browser.
  6. Without a connection string uploads continue to use local media. Existing local files are not automatically migrated. Signed Blob links expire; refresh the page to obtain a current link.
  7. After release, verify one project creation, one allocation, one staff update, an admin and Centre Head financial save, and an Overseer denial. Keep backup recovery and rollback procedures available.

Test runs and browser evidence use test_artifacts/test.db and a separate test-suite database; production migrations have not been run as part of this work. Browser session files remain outside the handover package. Stop disposable review servers when finished.

Known limitations and acceptance checklist

  • The demonstration allocation was saved, but the application displayed an email-delivery warning. Production email delivery requires separate environment verification.
  • Live Azure or Azurite uploads were not exercised in this run. The test settings use local storage.
  • Dean publication mutation buttons and the older Supervisor layout access mismatches from the earlier audit remain outside these requested role changes.
  • The local server reported missing image assets on some staff/student pages. Core pages returned 200; those cosmetic asset paths should be reviewed separately.
  • No load, penetration, disaster-recovery or real-user accessibility sign-off is claimed by this test result.

Before accepting the release, confirm the role matrix with business owners, verify staging email and storage, approve the financial exclusions for Overseer, and sign off the role-specific UAT journeys.
